sections.html:
Albany County's seat is Laramie, which counted 31,407 people and 13,554 households in the 2020 census. It sits at about 7,165 feet on the Laramie River, where Interstate 80 meets U.S. 287, roughly 50 miles from Cheyenne.

The University of Wyoming is the largest employer, with nearly 3,000 employees, and the median age of 27.2 is young for a Wyoming city. Plenty of Laramie houses are therefore rentals, so many sellers here are landlords rather than owner-occupants. Because one big institution anchors the job market, a shift at the university can ripple into local housing demand.

Laramie is high, dry and cold. Annual snowfall runs about 48 to 50 inches, and freezing temperatures are possible from September 14 through June 6. At that elevation, heating costs and the weight of snow on a roof are ordinary concerns for every owner.

The city building office publishes local design criteria such as snow loads, wind speeds, frost depth and seismic classification in its Bulletin #2. Expect a buyer to ask about the roof, insulation and furnace age, and have those answers ready.

Most residential projects and repairs in Laramie need a building permit. The city applies the 2024 International Building Code with local amendments in Laramie Municipal Code Chapter 15.24.

Code Administration lists work that does not need a permit:

  • One-story sheds and playhouses under 200 square feet that meet setbacks.
  • Fences up to 7 feet high in back and side yards only.
  • Retaining walls up to 4 feet high, measured from the bottom of the footing.
  • Unattached decks under 200 square feet that are no more than 30 inches above grade and do not serve the front door.
  • Painting, papering and similar finish work.

Applications are filed through the Civic Access online portal, and plan review is estimated at three weeks. Code Administration is at 406 Ivinson Avenue, phone 307-721-5271.

Zoning follows the Unified Development Code, which sets many districts and overlays, among them the Aquifer Protection Overlay and the Gateway Overlay. Planning prefers that owners reach out before buying, changing a use or dividing land. The Planning Division is at 320 E Grand Avenue, (307) 721-5207, or planning@cityoflaramie.org.

A finished basement, an old addition or a deck built without a permit is worth raising with Code Administration now. Learn what it would take to bring the work into compliance before a buyer's inspector spots it.

Wyoming sets one property tax calendar for all counties. The first half is due on or after September 1 and payable on or after November 10. The second half is due on or after March 1 and payable on or after May 10 of the following year. Pay the full amount by December 31 and no interest or penalty applies.

Late balances accrue interest at 18 percent per year. The Treasurer is at 307-721-2502 and the Assessor at 307-721-2511, and the county runs an online portal for looking up and paying bills. The courthouse is at 525 E Grand Avenue.

The Homeowner's Exemption cuts taxable value by 25 percent on the first $1 million of fair market value of a primary residence. A separate Long-term Homeowner's Exemption cuts it by 50 percent on the first $3 million for owners 65 or older with at least 25 years of Wyoming residential property tax payments. For tax year 2027, the owner must live in the home at least eight months of the year, and the County Assessor reviews each application.

If you sell during the year, the title company can tell you how the current bill is prorated.

The Albany County Clerk, reachable at 307-721-2541, records deeds and keeps grantor and grantee indexes. Wyoming Statute 18-3-402 directs the clerk to stamp every instrument with the day, hour and minute it arrives. The filing date becomes the date of record, and the clerk cannot record anything until the fee is paid.

Before you list, gather your recorded deed, any easements and any recorded agreements. A buyer who sees tidy paperwork has fewer reasons to hesitate.

sections.h2: What to have ready for a sale
sections.html:
Preparation shortens the path to closing. Bring the following to your title company or to a buyer:

  • Your recorded deed and any easements or recorded agreements.
  • Permit records, or a note of any work done without one.
  • A current tax balance from the Treasurer.
  • Your mortgage payoff statement, if there is a loan.
  • If the house is a rental, the lease and the planned move-out date.

Tenants are not a barrier to selling, but their lease terms shape the timing. Say so early so the closing date can be set around them.

sections.h2: When does a cash sale help a Laramie seller?
sections.html:
Sellers in Laramie often hold rental houses with put-off maintenance, inherited homes, or places that need roof or insulation work before a move. Cash makes sense if you want to skip repairs, open houses and a loan contingency.

Our offers reflect the house in its present state. We look at condition, location and the work a buyer would take on, then give you a number to accept or decline. No price is promised before we see the property.

  • Traditional listing: broader exposure and often a higher price, along with commission, repairs and a longer timeline.
  • Cash sale: fewer steps and a faster close, typically below the price of a prepared listing.

Tell us about back taxes, liens, tenants or a mortgage balance at the start. Those details change the closing steps and the paperwork the title company needs.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Laramie house as a rental with tenants in it?
faqs.a: Often yes, though lease terms and timing need to be reviewed. Tell us about the lease and the move-out date so we can plan the closing.

faqs.q: When are Albany County property taxes due?
faqs.a: First half is due September 1 and payable by November 10. Second half is due March 1 and payable by May 10. Paying everything by December 31 avoids interest, and the Treasurer at 307-721-2502 can confirm your balance.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for work on my Laramie house before selling?
faqs.a: Most residential projects and repairs need one, with exceptions for small sheds, low fences, short retaining walls and finish work. Call Code Administration at 307-721-5271 before starting. A permit is not required to sell, but unpermitted work can complicate a deal.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for a Laramie property?
faqs.a: With the Albany County Clerk at 307-721-2541. The clerk stamps the time of receipt and requires the fee up front.

faqs.q: Does winter affect selling a house in Laramie?
faqs.a: It can. About 48 to 50 inches of snow falls in a year, and freezing temperatures are possible from mid-September into early June. Schedule inspections and closings with that in mind.
